claim: You cannot change which AWS account is the management account of an organization, so AWS advises choosing it carefully.
question: Can the management account of an organization be changed to another account?

values.display: You cannot change which AWS account
select your management account carefully

evidence.quote: No. You cannot change which AWS account is the management account. Therefore, you should select your management account carefully.

claim: An AWS account can be a member of only one organization at a time.
question: Can one AWS account be a member of more than one organization at the same time?

values.display: member of only one organization at a time

evidence.quote: No. An AWS account can be a member of only one organization at a time.

claim: An AWS account can be a member of only one OU at a time.
question: Can an AWS account belong to more than one OU?

values.display: member of only one OU at a time

evidence.quote: No. An AWS account can be a member of only one OU at a time.

claim: An OU can be a member of only one OU at a time, so an OU cannot have more than one parent OU.
question: Can an OU be a member of more than one OU?

values.display: An OU can be a member of only one OU at a time

evidence.quote: No. An OU can be a member of only one OU at a time.

claim: The FAQ says you can nest OUs five levels deep, and that the whole hierarchy, counting the root and the accounts in the lowest OUs, can be five levels deep.
question: How many levels deep can the OU hierarchy of an organization be, according to the FAQ?

values.display: five levels deep

evidence.quote: You can nest your OUs five levels deep. Including root and AWS accounts created in the lowest OUs, your hierarchy can be five levels deep.

note: Possible scope conflict with organizations-ou-max-nesting-five-levels (user guide quota: five levels of OUs under a root). The FAQ counts the root and the accounts inside the five levels. Same number, so M12 does not queue it; the adjudicator should decide which wording the book teaches.

claim: All organization entities are global, not Regional, except for organizations managed in China; this is similar to how IAM works.
question: Is an organization defined and managed per Region, or is it global?

values.display: All organization entities are globally accessible

evidence.quote: All organization entities are globally accessible, except for organizations managed in China, similar to how AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) works today.

claim: You do not specify an AWS Region when you create and manage an organization, but accounts used in China need a separate organization.
question: Do you choose a Region when you create an organization, and what about accounts in China?

values.display: You do not need to specify an AWS Region
create a separate organization for accounts used in China

evidence.quote: You do not need to specify an AWS Region when you create and manage your organization, but you will need to create a separate organization for accounts used in China.

claim: Setting up MFA programmatically on an AWS account that you create in your organization is currently not supported, according to the FAQ.
question: Can MFA be set up programmatically on accounts created through Organizations?

values.display: This currently is not supported.

evidence.quote: This currently is not supported.

note: The quote answers the FAQ question 'Can I set up multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the AWS account that I create in my organization programmatically?' (the line above it).

claim: An AWS account created with AWS Organizations can be transferred to a new organization through an invitation, and after the new organization accepts, the account inherits that organization's billing, support plans and policies.
question: Can an account created with Organizations move to another organization, and what changes for it?

values.display: can be transferred to a new organization through an invitation process
inherit the new organization's billing, support plans, and policies

evidence.quote: Yes. AWS account you created using AWS Organizations can be transferred to a new organization through an invitation process.
Once invitation is accepted by the new Organization, your account will inherit the new organization's billing, support plans, and policies.

claim: An account created in an organization can be removed and made standalone, but because AWS did not collect all standalone-account information at creation, you must first add it, which can include contact information, a valid payment method and a support plan.
question: Can an account created with Organizations be removed and made a standalone account, and what must you add?

values.display: AWS does not collect all of the information required of standalone accounts
providing a valid payment method

evidence.quote: Yes. When you create an account in an organization using the AWS Organizations console, API, or CLI commands, AWS does not collect all of the information required of standalone accounts.

For each account that you want to make standalone, you need to update this information, which can include: providing contact information, providing a valid payment method, and choosing a support plan option.

claim: An administrator in the invited AWS account must accept or reject the invitation, through the Organizations console, the AWS CLI or the Organizations API.
question: Does an invited account join an organization automatically?

values.display: must accept or reject the request

evidence.quote: An administrator in the invited AWS account must accept or reject the request using the AWS Organizations console, AWS CLI, or Organizations API.

claim: When an account joins an organization, applicable policies such as SCPs are enforced in it automatically; for example an SCP attached to the root applies to the new account directly.
question: When an account joins an organization, when do the organization's SCPs start to apply to it?

values.display: will be enforced automatically in the newly added account

evidence.quote: Any applicable policies, such as SCPs, will be enforced automatically in the newly added account. For example, if your organization has an SCP attached to the root of your organization it will directly be enforced on the newly created accounts.

claim: After you add an account, by invitation or by creation, you can move it to an OU, and the account automatically inherits the policies attached to that OU.
question: What happens to the policies of an account that you move into an OU?

values.display: automatically inherits the policies attached to the OU

evidence.quote: For both methods, after you add the new account, you can move it to an organizational unit (OU). The new account automatically inherits the policies attached to the OU.

claim: You can invite more than one AWS account in one action by giving a comma-separated list of email addresses or AWS account IDs.
question: Can you invite several accounts to an organization at once?

values.display: comma-separated list of email addresses or AWS account IDs

evidence.quote: Note: You can invite more than one AWS account by providing a comma-separated list of email addresses or AWS account IDs.

claim: The FAQ says the number of accounts you can manage in an organization can vary, and that you request more accounts by opening a support case in the AWS Support Center.
question: How do you get more accounts in an organization, according to the FAQ?

values.display: open a support case to request an increase

evidence.quote: This can vary. If you need additional accounts, go to the AWS Support Center and open a support case to request an increase.

note: The user guide quota page (organizations-max-accounts-default-10) says the quota is adjusted through the Service Quotas console; the FAQ says a support case. Writers should follow the user guide for the current method.

claim: To remove a member account from an organization, from the management account or from the member account, the account must have a valid payment method, and you must provide one if it does not.
question: What must a member account have before it can be removed from an organization?

values.display: you must provide one

evidence.quote: If the account does not have a valid payment method, you must provide one.

claim: You can create and manage an organization without enforcing any SCP: you decide which policies to enforce, and an organization can use only consolidated billing.
question: Can an organization be created and managed without enforcing any SCP?

values.display: You decide which policies that you want to enforce
only of the consolidated billing functionality

evidence.quote: Yes. You decide which policies that you want to enforce. For example, you could create an organization that takes advantage only of the consolidated billing functionality.

claim: Consolidated billing gives an organization a single payer account for all its accounts and default tiered-pricing benefits automatically.
question: What does consolidated billing give an organization?

values.display: single-payer account for all accounts
default tiered-pricing benefits

evidence.quote: This allows you to have a single-payer account for all accounts in your organization and automatically receive default tiered-pricing benefits.

claim: The bill of an organization does not reflect the OU structure that you defined.
question: Does the bill of an organization reflect its OU structure?

values.display: your bill will not reflect the structure

evidence.quote: No. For now, your bill will not reflect the structure that you have defined in your organization.

claim: To group costs, you can use cost allocation tags in individual accounts, and that allocation is visible in the consolidated bill of the organization.
question: How can an organization report costs by group when the bill does not follow OUs?

values.display: use cost allocation tags in individual AWS accounts

evidence.quote: You can use cost allocation tags in individual AWS accounts to categorize and track your AWS costs, and this allocation will be visible in the consolidated bill for your organization.

claim: AWS Organizations has no additional charge.
question: What does AWS Organizations cost?

values.display: offered at no additional charge

evidence.quote: AWS Organizations is offered at no additional charge.

claim: The owner of the management account pays for all usage, data and resources used by the accounts in the organization.
question: Who pays for the usage of member accounts in an organization?

values.display: responsible for paying for all usage, data, and resources

evidence.quote: The owner of the management account is responsible for paying for all usage, data, and resources used by the accounts in the organization.

claim: An RCP can restrict access to your resources so that only identities in your organization can access them, or set the conditions under which external identities can access them.
question: What is a typical use of a resource control policy (RCP)?

values.display: only be accessed by identities that belong to your organization

evidence.quote: For example, an RCP can help restrict access to your resources so that they can only be accessed by identities that belong to your organization, or specifying the conditions under which identities external to your organization can access your resources.

claim: Using multiple AWS accounts is a best practice for scaling, because accounts give a natural billing boundary and isolate resources for security.
question: Why does AWS call multiple accounts a best practice?

values.display: natural billing boundary for costs
isolates resources for security

evidence.quote: Using multiple AWS accounts is a best practice for scaling your environment, as it provides a natural billing boundary for costs, isolates resources for security, gives flexibility or individuals and teams, in addition to being adaptable for new business processes.
